generations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a LANDSCAPE WIDE architectural evolution sheet, aspect ratio 3:1, five equal-width vertical panels in ONE horizontal row. Five panels exactly, no text, no numbers, no captions. Each panel is the same fixed 3/4 view of the same charming house and the SAME little patchwork teddy Pokomoko. Each panel must have identical world scale, camera elevation, orientation, ground baseline, door landing location, and bear size. Do NOT enlarge the early house to fill its panel. Use a quiet pale mint/ivory seamless background, a small grass base, minimal props, not an island or busy landscape. The largest final house fits fully inside its panel with margins; smaller early houses have more empty space. NOT five different houses.
Input 1 is MATERIAL + HOUSE ID reference only: cream painted wood walls, BLUE round-top front door with tiny flower medallion, white round crossbar window, broad ceramic scalloped ROSE PINK/YELLOW/COBALT roof tiles, chunky chimney. Input 2 exact hero identity: ivory LEFT / cobalt RIGHT face, yellow center seam, navy left ear cream dots, pink right ear cream dots, ivory muzzle, small dark eyes/nose, cream/navy striped and yellow torso, turquoise/pink arms, short plush legs. Same bear full body beside front path in identical pose and size in all five panels. Hero small, approx one door tall. No substitute bear or additional characters.
Progression LEFT TO RIGHT:
1 A genuinely SMALL delightful one-room cottage: one simple gable, one doorway, one small circular window, chimney. No porch roof, upper wing, balcony, greenhouse, climbing vines or elaborate flowers. One tiny planter only.
2 SAME cottage plus a shallow timber canopy over entrance and simple flower window box. Core door and original gable remain. Still one storey, no broad terrace.
3 SAME cottage with a spacious wooden SIDE TERRACE and clear wood railing, little table and two chairs, canopy over terrace. No second floor yet. Clear lateral expansion of home, same core doorway.
4 SAME home and terrace, plus a clearly taller UPPER STOREY / attic with recognizable dormer room and side upper window. Meaningful taller silhouette. Original doorway, lower house and terrace remain.
5 SAME full home with attic/upper room and terrace, plus a DISTINCT elegant GLASS GREENHOUSE on the side, warm timber frames, a few plants visibly inside, richer roof edging and flower boxes. Clearly grander and wider but still home-like, not a castle. No gratuitous gold or jewels.
All 5 should look progressively substantial at constant object scale, not just differing flower quantity. Architectural changes must read at thumbnail size. Materials: ceramic tiles, painted wood, clear glass, natural grass and stone, ONLY bear is woven plush. High-end bright handcrafted 3D toy-world rendering, clean daylight, no heavy bokeh. Avoid carpet of flowers, enlarged trees, random decoration, excessive ivy, UI, diagrams, arrows, text, watermarks. This is a design comparison of home levels, not runtime screenshots.

Use case: identity-preserve. ONE landscape 3:2 GARDEN PROGRESSION SHEET with THREE equally sized panels side by side. No lettering, labels, numbers, captions, UI. Each panel uses the identical elevated 3/4 camera and world scale. Input 1 is the approved-for-study five-house progression: use ONLY the very first smallest cottage in EVERY panel, unchanged. Input 2 exact Pokomoko identity. This sheet changes garden objects ONLY, not the house.
The same small cream cottage with round blue door, round window, single colorful pink/yellow/blue ceramic tile gable and chunky chimney is near rear center of each little garden. Same Pokomoko standing in same spot next to front path at exact same scale and pose all panels, cream left face cobalt right face yellow seam, navy/pink dotted ears, striped/yellow torso and turquoise/pink arms. Quiet pale ivory/mint studio background, grass patch with same boundary and stone path, no island ocean or town. Camera fully contains final tree canopy; early objects NOT enlarged to fill their allotted area.
Lock positions of the FOUR garden items in all panels: a flower bed front-left, a purple tree rear-right, a bench under the tree mid-right, a lamp by path front-right. No extra items across panels.
LEFT early garden: about 75% clear short green grass, one small flower patch with three flower plants and some buds, small purple sapling whose canopy is shorter than cottage roof, plain simple wooden bench, short simple lamp. A delightful lived-in beginning, not barren or sad. No flower carpets, vines, fences, hanging planters, mature bush masses.
MIDDLE growing garden: same bounded flower bed with several flowers at mixed heights, medium purple tree with denser canopy, same bench with clear backrest and a little seat cushion, taller lamp with shade. Preserve plenty of clear ground, original cottage unchanged.
RIGHT full garden: same flower bed shape now richly blooming at varied heights (NOT whole ground covered), full rounded purple tree canopy, finely finished bench with carved timber details and cushions, handsome lamp with decorative but simple architectural silhouette. Garden footprint unchanged, path remains clear and all props usable. At most 30% of ground visually occupied by planting; do not fill all corners with flowers.
Style: match tactile sunny handcrafted 3D reference: painted wood, ceramic, stone, small grass, translucent lamp glass, only hero is woven plush. Main difference is graduated silhouettes/material detail, same object identity all stages. No extra trees or characters, no confetti or sparkles. Do not turn the lamp into a magical object. Concept design, not screenshots.

Use case: identity-preserve. Make ONE LANDSCAPE 2:1 comparison sheet, exactly THREE equal tall portrait panels side by side. Each panel depicts the SAME island at an identical world scale, fixed camera, horizon, lighting, house front door ground position, hero position and original front dock. No text, no numbers, no captions/UI. Do not zoom in on the initial island or zoom out on the mature one. Earlier smaller island leaves more sea around and behind it. Entire front and side coasts readable, not cropped by frame.
Input 1 HOUSE progression is authoritative for architecture: use its panel 1 house in LEFT island, its panel 3 terrace house in MIDDLE island, and its panel 5 clearly two-storey house with greenhouse in RIGHT island. Input 2 GARDEN progression is authoritative for density: use garden stage1/2/3 respectively. Input 3 previous mature island is composition/material inspiration only; do not copy its excess flower carpeting or its less developed house. Input 4 exact identity of Pokomoko. Hero is a cream-left/cobalt-right patchwork teddy, yellow center seam, navy dotted left and pink dotted right ears, tiny dark eyes/nose, ivory muzzle, striped/yellow torso, turquoise/pink arms. Hero must remain same body proportions, size and position in all panels near home; no pink left-face recoloring.
Camera is high enough to see island depth but low enough to recognize bear. Home is front-lower-left/center, largest focal building, full porch/roof visible. Original dock at lower-left, curved sandy shore around foreground, purple tree to home's right. Ocean vivid turquoise/cobalt, horizon at same height. Permanent fixed front dock, shoreline rocks, front path and doorway. Land growth happens BEHIND the original garden.
LEFT: genuinely humble delightful beginning, small one-room cottage from house1, one little flower bed, small purple tree, simple bench and short lamp. NO greenhouse, upper room, roofed terrace, shop, park, distant developed land. Clear green grass about 70% of garden, no blanket of flowers. Pokomoko and one cream rabbit. Small connected island ends behind home, blue sea beyond.
MIDDLE: terrace house3, garden2, slightly longer continuous island extending behind home to ONE little shop and a simple park/bench, connected stone paths. One otter bringing a basket toward home. No greenhouse, upper storey, lighthouse, large harbor, observatory or waterwheel factory yet. Preserve grassy breathing room between plantings.
RIGHT: house5 has unmistakable full upper storey with dormer AND glass greenhouse beside terrace, garden3 still clear paths and breathing room, not wildflower carpet. Island much broader and deeper behind home, real continuous land and paths connecting a charming shop, a park, waterwheel workshop, harbor with one SMALL unbranded sailboat and a modest lighthouse, distant observatory secondary. Small rabbit/otter/fox residents live and carry things, never competing with hero. Home retains primacy over all background buildings. Lavender broad tree crowns, small bounded flower beds, benches and lamps. Clear differences in density, shape and living uses, not pure ornament clutter.
Art: refined handcrafted stylized 3D, real material differences of wood, ceramic tiles, glass, grass, stone, clear water, plush only for residents. Soft sunny daylight with crisp full-depth focus. Fixed noon sky, no sunsets or season changes. No camera shift, no halos, confetti, logos, flags with pictograms, labels, menus, or render watermarks. Concept sequence, not implementation screenshots.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this exact three-panel progression sheet. Keep the middle and right panels unchanged as closely as possible, and keep the left panel house, hero, rabbit, front dock, foreground coast, sky, camera, scale and lighting unchanged. Fix ONLY the early-garden planting in the LEFT panel: replace the large purple tree beside the left house with a much smaller young tree at the exact same root position, with canopy top BELOW the house roof apex and a visibly narrow rounded purple crown; replace the tall streetlamp by a short simple lantern at same position; reduce extra flower bushes outside the small single flower planter to clear short grass. Remove three large conifer trees behind the left house and leave simple natural grass with at most one low bush, so early garden is mostly open inviting green ground, not lush mature planting. Preserve charming cozy appearance; do not make it dead, damaged or barren. NO other changes. Three panels, no text. Do not change character identity or regenerate the other stages. Output same landscape 2:1 ratio.
